body: Neurodiversity ↗ refers to the infinite variation in human minds. The neurodiversity paradigm is the perspective that there's no "right" way for a mind to function, and the neurodiversity movement seeks civil rights, equality & inclusion for neurodivergent folks. Psychology & psychiatry have a long history of being on the wrong side of this, causing harms to neurodivergent folks through pathologisation, eugenics, and institutionalisation. Black feminist disability justice gives us a framework to address these harms, and participatory approaches invite us to rethink the way we do research. Here are some resources on the topic: #### Neurodiversity in academia A workshop co-organised with Mira Nencheva, Laura Murray, and Laura Bustamante for the Princeton University Neurodiversity Collective ↗. Discusses past & current harms, a history of neurodiversity movements, and where academia is now in terms of legislation, accommodations, and disclosure. Followed by a lived experience panel and breakouts on participatory research and teaching. Slides ↗ #### Neurodiversity resource guide for scientists A resource guide written with Charlie Rodriguez-Deliz and the Scientist Action and Advocacy Network ↗, by neurodivergent scientists for the broader scientific community: what neurodiversity and disability mean, disability rights as civil rights, why this concerns scientists, community-based participatory research, identity-first language, and re-evaluating interventions like ABA. PDF ↗ #### Season of the Bitch, ep. 185: Freud is the worst A podcast episode ↗ on the history of psychology & psychiatry: Freud, the pathologisation of Black, queer, trans and neurodivergent people, carceral aspects of the mental health system, and non-carceral alternatives like peer support. #### #StopTheShock campaign The Judge Rotenberg Center in Massachusetts still uses electric shock devices on disabled residents. The FDA banned the devices in 2020, but a federal court overturned the ban in 2021. Congress restored the FDA's authority in 2022 and the FDA re-proposed the ban in 2024, but missed its own deadline to finalise it in 2026. Campaign page ↗ from the Autistic Self Advocacy Network.

Hi, I'm Sashank! I'm a research scientist with 10+ years of experience studying the failure modes of intelligent systems. Currently, I work on model behaviour & alignment of open-weight models at **Reflection** ↗. Previously, I lead the research team at Atla training general-purpose evaluators ↗, prior to which I was at Limbic building safety guardrails ↗ for mental health applications. Before that, I was a postdoc at Princeton studying continual learning failures ↗ in psychotherapy, following my PhD in computational neuroscience studying lapses ↗ in decision-making. I enjoy making music and writing poems ↗. email: firstname[dot]lastname[at]gmail.com

A few selected poems. The rest are on wordpress ↗. ### sunflower sweater weather.

sunrises     aren’t     overrated
but  rising  to  your  glowing
countenance from the depths
of dreamland is far more
like living the dream.

### peel/new commuter poem

Cork and mottle, cork and sheaf
Pale red, white, and bottled beef.
Wrapped like pastry, foreground trees
Gig workers on metal sheets.
Skies cross down on ocean feet
Fried potatoes, boiled reef.
Water current,
Current grief,
Past present and future teeth
Words abundant, concerns brief,
Water fresh, fresh water thief
Flowers, dresses in the pink
Hearts disabled, bodies bleak
Well lit tunnels, well lit streets
Wealthy neighbours, plastic wreaths
Plastic neighbours, shiny seats
Tables empty, clean, and neat.
Clear conditions, airline breeze
Airways blocked by carried wheeze
Whose ending, and whose reprise?
Whose blank page and whose skin seized?

### sooth & nail

hold fast my skin,
contain what’s within me;
don’t open up steaming
on water or whim

something beneath
fast pulsing or breathing,
stuck under a nail bed
of hands or my feet

sitting at home
but home once forgotten,
I peer inside of my being
fibre and bone

structured and dry,
a plan of a plan I see
patiently screaming
this mouth or an eye

something distracts
there in the ground I keep
plastic syringe I must
throw away fast

was it not pain?
no, tenderness at worst
exposed and sweating
but fearless frame

pores open wide
visceral feeling
inviting me gently to
see what’s inside

see sooth, and say
what this partial membrane
holds within and without
not seance but song

clear as the night
watery organs
not full moon, not half dog
but sobering light

two birds, two stones
council of matriarchs
skeleton woman
from dreams long ago

what did she say?
nothing at all at first,
looks of assurance
I’m not going away

and in this dream
not in a dungeon, no
sitting up, I awake
surrogate stream

hold fast my skin,
I know what’s within me;
a channel, a river bed
water and whim.

### ephemera.

I catch my reflection in the dusty window pane of a passing train,
Preen, vain, window, pain;
Staring, starring, stardust too caught up in the brilliance of its own fast burn;
Mesmerized, vaporized.
A moment of recognition, of self, of identity, and immediately of vanity
Self, selfish. Consciousness? No, how can I be conscious when I am so confident?
I confide in myself; sometimes this makes me feel powerful, sometimes overpowered
Not conscious of myself, not conscious at all, only consummate, luscious, copious
A flick of the hair, like a comet’s tail
A tilt of the hip, like a
Beckoning (come hither)
Echo
The sounds of my own voice
Writhing about, writing about myself
Gotta get it out.
Why is there such a fine line between self love and self loathing?
To be loved by myself is intoxicating, overbearing
Love, self.

### Flowers, dancing & weak knees

Dollop of honey,
Slow teardrop, sweet, sour memory
Of a thousand trips.
